title: Sharp maximum graph dimension as a function of (n, m)

problemStatement.formal: Determine the exact extremal function D(n,m) = max { dim(G) : |V(G)| = n, |E(G)| = m }, where dim(G) is the least d with a unit-distance embedding G -> R^d, sharpening the known brackets D(n,m) <= min(n-1, 2m) (with D(n, C(n,2)) = n-1 realized by K_n).
problemStatement.plain: A graph's dimension is the fewest Euclidean coordinates needed to place its vertices so that adjacent ones are exactly one unit apart. Complete graphs need n-1 dimensions and no n-vertex graph needs more, while an m-edge graph never needs more than 2m. This problem asks for the exact largest dimension once both the vertex count n and edge count m are fixed, and which graph families attain it, closing the gap between the n-1 and 2m bounds.
whyMatters: It is the concrete extremal core of Erdos Problem #1007 (open question OQ-04): dimension as a function of the pair (n, m), not of n alone.

A sharp D(n,m) would unify the sporadic exact results known only for small target dimensions (House 2013 for dimension 4, Chaffee-Noble 2016 for dimension 5) into a single global formula and quantify how geometrically complex a sparse graph can be.

proven: dim(K_n) = n-1 via the regular simplex (gallery erdos-1007-oq-01), the tight upper corner D(n, C(n,2)).
Subgraph monotonicity and the edge-count bound dim(G) <= 2m (gallery erdos-1007-oq-04, handshake lemma on the non-isolated support).
Chromatic bound dim(G) <= chi(G) <= n, so bipartite graphs embed in R^2 (gallery erdos-1007-oq-04).
Sharp small-dimension thresholds: a 4-dimensional graph has at least 9 edges with K_{3,3} the unique minimizer (House 2013); the dimension-5 analogue (Chaffee-Noble 2016).
open: The exact value of D(n,m) for general (n,m): a closed form interpolating between the n-1 and 2m regimes.
The extremal graph families attaining D(n,m) in the sparse regime m = o(n^2).
The sharp constant in the edge-count direction (improving 2m, and the truth for triangle-free / bipartite graphs).
knownResults.goal: Tighten and formalize the brackets rather than the full closed form: (a) prove an improved sparse-regime upper bound (e.g. in terms of the non-isolated support or chromatic/degeneracy number), and (b) formalize a concrete extremal family (such as K_{s,t} or disjoint simplex unions) with dimension provably above any constant while m = o(n^2), pinning down the order of magnitude of D(n,m) on a nontrivial slice.

papers: Erdos, Harary, Tutte, On the dimension of a graph, Mathematika 12 (1965), 118-122
House, A 4-dimensional graph has at least 9 edges, Discrete Mathematics 313(18) (2013), 1783-1789
